app.name: Shop
app.summary: Customers check out a cart on the web app and pay by card. Paid orders ship from one or more warehouses, and every night the day's orders are invoiced.

glossary.meaning: A paid cart. Created only after the card is charged.
What one warehouse sends for an order. An order can have several.
Issued every night for the previous day's orders.

flows.title: Open the checkout
flows.summary: What the customer sees on the checkout page: sent to sign in, an empty cart, or the payment form with a free-shipping banner.

calls.note: React Router runs the requireCustomer loader, then renders CheckoutPage

nodes.label: Is the customer signed in?
nodes.rule: Signed-out visitors are sent to sign in, and come back to the checkout afterwards.

nodes.label: Read the cart saved in the browser
nodes.rule: The cart lives in the browser until the order is placed.

nodes.label: Does the cart have items?
nodes.rule: An empty cart shows a message and a link back to the shop instead of the form.

nodes.label: Is the cart $99 or more?
nodes.rule: The banner promises free shipping from $99. Under that, it says how much more to add.

nodes.label: Checkout says "Free shipping on this order"

findings.text: The screen promises free shipping from $99, but the API ("Place an order") gives it from $100. A $99.50 cart is told shipping is free, then charged $7.90.

flows.title: Pay for the order
flows.summary: The customer presses Pay. The address is checked on the screen, the order is sent to the API, and the screen reacts to its answer.

calls.note: react-hook-form validates with the zod schema before calling pay

nodes.label: Is the delivery address complete?
nodes.rule: Name required, street of 3+ characters, a 5-digit postal code, and a country of US or Canada.

nodes.label: Is the order already being sent?
nodes.rule: The Pay button is disabled while the order is sent, and a second press is ignored. This stops double orders from a double click.

nodes.label: Send the order to the API
nodes.rule: The Pay button stays disabled until the API answers.

calls.note: sends the address and the session token

emits.label: the cart is read from the session on the API

nodes.label: What did the API answer?
nodes.rule: Each answer is handled by its status code. Any code not listed gets the same generic message.

nodes.label: Toast: "Your card was declined. Try another card."
Toast with the API's message (an item is out of stock)
Toast: "Something went wrong, please try again."
nodes.rule: Shown for every other answer: an empty cart (400), payments unavailable (503), and the generic 500, including when the card was charged but the order was not saved.

nodes.label: Errors shown under the address fields
Pay button stays disabled, no message
nodes.rule: If the request itself fails (offline, timeout), the error is not caught. The button is never enabled again and the customer is not told anything. Reloading the page is the only way out.

findings.text: When the API charged the card but could not save the order, the screen says "please try again". Trying again charges the card a second time.
The Pay button shows the cart total without shipping. Under $100 the card is charged $7.90 more than the button says.
The shop ships to Canada, but the postal code must be 5 digits. No Canadian postal code (like K1A 0B1) can pass, so Canadian customers cannot check out.
If the request fails, the Pay button stays disabled and the customer is told nothing.

flows.title: Place an order
flows.summary: A signed-in customer checks out their cart. Stock is checked, shipping is added, the card is charged (with retries), the order is saved and sent to shipping.

calls.note: Express route, runs requireCustomer then placeOrder

nodes.label: Is the customer signed in?
nodes.rule: Only a signed-in customer can place an order.

nodes.label: Does the cart have items?
nodes.rule: An empty cart cannot be ordered.

nodes.label: Is every item in stock?
nodes.rule: Each item is checked one by one with the inventory service. The first item without enough stock stops the order. Stock is only checked, not reserved.

nodes.label: Is the order $100 or more?
nodes.rule: Orders of $100 or more ship for free.

nodes.label: Ship for free
nodes.rule: Shipping is $0.

nodes.label: Add $7.90 shipping
nodes.rule: Orders under $100 pay $7.90 shipping.

nodes.label: Charge the card
nodes.rule: Charges the cart total plus shipping.

nodes.label: Was the payment approved?
nodes.rule: Approved continues. Declined stops the order. Any other answer from the provider is treated as a temporary failure and retried.

nodes.label: Any payment attempts left?
nodes.rule: Up to 3 attempts in total.

nodes.label: Wait, then try again
nodes.rule: Waits 1 second after the first failure and 2 seconds after the second.

nodes.label: Asked to sign in
nodes.response: 401 · Sign in to place an order

nodes.label: Refused: an item is out of stock
Generic error: inventory did not answer
nodes.rule: The code does not handle an inventory timeout. The error escapes and Express answers with its default 500 page.

nodes.label: Payments unavailable
nodes.response: 503 · Payments are unavailable, try again later

nodes.label: Card charged, but no order saved
nodes.rule: If saving the order fails, the card has already been charged. Nothing refunds it and the customer sees a generic error.

findings.text: If saving the order fails after the card is charged, the customer pays and gets no order. Nothing refunds them.
Stock is checked but not reserved, so two customers can both buy the last unit.
Any payment answer other than "approved" or "declined" (for example "pending review") is retried, which may charge the customer again.
An inventory timeout shows the customer a generic error page instead of a message.
The checkout screen promises free shipping from $99 (see "Open the checkout"), but this rule gives it from $100. A $99.50 cart is told shipping is free, then charged $7.90.

flows.title: Ship a paid order
flows.summary: Runs for every paid order. Each warehouse holding items gets its shipment request at the same time. When all have accepted, the order is marked shipped and the customer gets the tracking links.

nodes.label: Was the order cancelled?
nodes.rule: Cancelled orders are skipped.

nodes.label: Split the order by warehouse
nodes.rule: One shipment per warehouse that holds items of the order. All are requested at the same time.

fanout.over: one shipment per warehouse, all at once

nodes.label: Ask the warehouse to ship its items
Did every warehouse accept?
nodes.rule: Waits for every warehouse. A single rejection fails the whole job.

nodes.label: Does the queue have retries left?
nodes.rule: The queue runs the whole job again, up to 5 attempts in total, waiting longer each time (about 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes).

nodes.label: Job fails for good; nobody is told
nodes.rule: After the 5th failure the job stays in the queue's failed list. The order stays "paid", and no one is alerted.

findings.text: A retry asks every warehouse again, including the ones that already accepted. One failing warehouse can create up to 5 duplicate shipments elsewhere.
When the job gives up, the order stays "paid" forever and nobody is alerted.

flows.title: Invoice the day's orders
flows.summary: Every night, orders without an invoice are invoiced in batches of 100. Within a batch, all invoices are issued at the same time.

nodes.label: Read the next 100 orders without an invoice

fanout.over: uninvoiced orders, 100 per batch, one batch after another

nodes.label: Any orders left?
nodes.rule: The run ends when a batch comes back empty.

nodes.label: Issue the batch's invoices at the same time

fanout.over: every order in the batch (up to 100)

nodes.label: Were all invoices in the batch issued?
nodes.rule: Waits for every invoice in the batch. One failure stops the whole run.

nodes.label: All of the day's orders are invoiced
Run stops halfway
nodes.rule: An invoice failure is not handled. The run stops, the remaining orders wait until the next night, and the batch is not marked as invoiced.

findings.text: When one invoice fails, the others in its batch were already issued but are not marked. The next night issues them again: customers get duplicate invoices.
Nobody is alerted when the run stops halfway.
